producer_report.summary: Changed D87's intervention signal from class docs to class code. Added derived host-error records. HostError gets `derived` (bool) and `source_intervention`, both left out when serialized for observed records. Validation requires a source exactly when `derived` is true. `derive_host_error` in watcher.rs returns a record only when the intervention's what+why contain `HTTP ` plus a three-digit code from 100 to 599 and the word merge/merges/merged, and the intervention names a job. The record uses operation merge, phase landing, and the intervention's id, time and job. The backtest builds these in memory (nothing under records/), keeps them apart from observed records, and the report lists them as derived and not observed by the client. D87's citation reads "<id> (derived, not observed; from intervention <src>)". I did not get the real result for criterion 6: this working copy has no records/ directory, so `cargo run -q -p athena-cli -- backtest` read 0 jobs and 0 interventions. It exited 2 with finding (b): D87 had 0 jobs against a threshold of 2 and did not fire; D88 has no runnable signal; nothing else was flagged. Running the same command in the real repository will give the real D87/ar1x result. Judged by the new fixture test, D87 should fire through a derived record citing ar1x if ar1x's text states HTTP 405 and a merge and it names a job. Existing backtest fixtures were switched docs to code. Docs: a new section in decision-sets.md §9 and a CHANGELOG entry.

checks_run.note: Ran with -q; every result line was ok. New tests: derivation (match, non-match, no job, out-of-range code), record validation, and two backtest fixtures (HTTP 405 on a merge flags D87 through a derived record; no such text flags nothing).
This copy has no records/, so it reported 0 jobs and 0 interventions and exited 2 with finding (b). It does not show the real D87 result.

open_issues: The real D87 result needs a run in the real repository with records/; I could not do it. The derivation also needs ar1x's intervention to be a valid AnyRecord and to name a job; otherwise nothing is derived.

A derived record reuses the intervention's id as its own id; the derived marker is what tells it apart. If an observed record for the same refusal later exists, both would fire; I added no de-duplication.
The live watcher's evaluate() does not ignore derived records, but none are ever committed, so it never sees one.
store.rs and decisions.rs from the deliverables list needed no change.
mistakes: I first put the derived sort before the on-disk host-error read, then moved it to the end of read_records.
I first added a duplicate '### Added' heading to the CHANGELOG, then merged my entries under the existing one.
learnings: records/ is absent from the producer snapshot, so the real backtest cannot be exercised here.

RecordId suffixes use Crockford base32, so test ids like 'i001' may not parse as RecordId; the existing backtest rows parse loosely, so I kept the row read as before and derive only when the full AnyRecord::parse succeeds.
